texts.orig: With this very basic framework, you’ll immediately identify 80-90% of your best opportunities and, more important, have a starting point for conversations with your team and team leads. Expect to adjust this list by 10-20% based on dependencies, hard-to-quantify opinions, and other strategic priorities.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I’ve tried so many frameworks over the years, constantly hoping to make the process less subjective. But again and again, I’ve found that there’s no way to avoid the messiness of people, opinions, and unknowns. Instead, I embrace the messiness and keep the process simple and people-focused.
texts.text: I’ve tried so many frameworks over the years, constantly hoping to make the process less subjective. But again and again, I’ve found that there’s no way to avoid the messiness of people, opinions, and unknowns. Instead, I embrace the messiness and keep the process simple and people-focused.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For that reason, I prefer using T-shirt sizes instead of a 1-5 rating (which many people prefer) because it forces me to manually sort the list, and thus keeps me from expecting a magical math formula to give me the answers.

texts.orig: How does strategy fit into this process?
texts.text: How does strategy fit into this process?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Do not prioritize your roadmap until you have a strategy.
texts.text: Do not prioritize your roadmap until you have a strategy.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Developing a roadmap without a strategy is like heading into battle without a plan.
texts.text: Developing a roadmap without a strategy is like heading into battle without a plan.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your prioritization needs to be driven by your Goals/KPIs, which come from your Strategy, which are rooted in your Mission/Vision. It’s all connected 🌀
texts.text: Your prioritization needs to be driven by your Goals/KPIs, which come from your Strategy, which are rooted in your Mission/Vision. It’s all connected 🌀

texts.orig: How do I prioritize small bets vs. big bets?
texts.text: How do I prioritize small bets vs. big bets?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you did your product strategy correctly, you will have identified 2-5 strategic bets your company/team plans to focus on for the next month/quarter/year. These are sometimes called strategic pillars, bets, or swimlanes.
texts.text: If you did your product strategy correctly, you will have identified 2-5 strategic bets your company/team plans to focus on for the next month/quarter/year. These are sometimes called strategic pillars, bets, or swimlanes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Next, your leaders should have decided roughly what percent of available resources they want to put into each of these pillars/bets/swimlanes. Let’s say:
texts.text: Next, your leaders should have decided roughly what percent of available resources they want to put into each of these pillars/bets/swimlanes. Let’s say:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Great! Everyone now knows how much focus each of these bets will receive.
texts.text: Great! Everyone now knows how much focus each of these bets will receive.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Now, within each of these strategic bets, you can start to mix small and big bets. I like to follow the 80/20 rule: Roughly 80% of resources go to incremental low-risk projects, and 20% go to longer-term higher-risk bets. Kind of like this:
texts.text: Now, within each of these strategic bets, you can start to mix small and big bets. I like to follow the 80/20 rule: Roughly 80% of resources go to incremental low-risk projects, and 20% go to longer-term higher-risk bets. Kind of like this:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Take on too many long-term big bets, and leaders will wonder why you aren’t moving your metrics (and will often pull your resources). Take on too much incremental work, and you’ll never break out of a local maximum.
texts.text: Take on too many long-term big bets, and leaders will wonder why you aren’t moving your metrics (and will often pull your resources). Take on too much incremental work, and you’ll never break out of a local maximum.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I like to think of low-risk incremental bets as creating cover-fire for your big long-term bets, by moving your KPIs and showing success while you continue to make forward progress on your big ambitious bets behind the scenes🛡
texts.text: I like to think of low-risk incremental bets as creating cover-fire for your big long-term bets, by moving your KPIs and showing success while you continue to make forward progress on your big ambitious bets behind the scenes🛡
